body.statement: For each fixed \(0<\alpha<1\), under \(d^{\mathrm{pre}}_{n,B}\), \[\sup_{1\le B\le\lfloor n/4\rfloor}\sup_{(\mu,\sigma)\in\Theta}\left|P^{d^{\mathrm{pre}}_{n,B}}_{\mu,\sigma}\{\tau\in\mathcal I_{n,B}(\alpha)\}-(1-\alpha)\right|\to0.\] Moreover, \(\widehat Q_{n,B}\) is uniformly ratio-consistent for the predictable variance of \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{d^{\mathrm{pre}}_{n,B}}-\tau)\), and the corresponding studentized statistic converges uniformly to \(\mathcal N(0,1)\).
body.justification: A frontier without valid uncertainty quantification would not support a production cadence decision.
body.gap: Zhang, Janson, and Murphy fix the batch count and grow every batch, while adaptive AIPW results use per-unit Bernoulli policies; neither covers this exact-count, potentially small-cell frontier family.
body.consumer: The same batch outputs used to choose the update cadence yield a fixed-time confidence interval for the ATE.
